findings.title: The round's own arm table says the retired arm's way back is a restatement "(#721's door admits it)" -- measured, that door REFUSES a retired Work; the shipped surfaces are right, the record is not
findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_l09, driving the real doors. A Work parked on a question, no committed receipt, retired by a correction of the document it cites: status `stopping`, question `cancelled`, `clara.get_work_question` -> `work_posted=false`, `source_corrected_at` set. `clara.restate_accounting_work` against it returns `CLR13 {"reason":"not_restatable","status":"stopping"}` -- 0200's door only admits queued/running/awaiting_input, and the cancellation has already moved it out. So `wave2-lane09-fix.md`'s third-round table row ("retired Work (question cancelled) | convergeSourceCorrected | restate is the way back (#721's door admits it)") is false on its second and third columns' joint claim. THE SHIPPED CODE IS CORRECT AND THIS IS WHY THE SEVERITY IS MINOR: the sentence never names a restatement -- `convergeSourceCorrected` ends "the instruction has to be given again on the corrected document", which a new admission satisfies -- and no surface offers a control that would refuse, because `offersRestateFor` is already false on that arm for an independent reason (`work_status === 'awaiting_input'` fails at `stopping`; measured false with `offerRestate=true`, `basis` present, `work_posted=false`). The carve-out arm by contrast names a control that really works: `convergeSourceCorrectedPosted` says "use Cancel Work", `offersRestateFor` is false via the new `work_posted` conjunct, `restate_accounting_work` refuses `not_restatable status=completed`, and `clara.cancel_agent_task` is ACCEPTED. The retired arm has no control of its own anywhere near the sentence, which is defensible (the person starts new work elsewhere) but is not what the table says.
findings.required_fix: Correct that one table row in `wave2-lane09-fix.md`: on the retired arm the restatement door refuses too (`not_restatable`, status `stopping`), no surface offers restate there, and "give the instruction again" means a fresh admission rather than a #721 restatement. No code change. Worth saying out loud because this is the third round in which a door's behaviour was asserted in the record without being driven -- the same class as the pin literal.

findings.title: The no-op guard catches only an edit that is equal under its own rule; a cosmetically-equivalent edit still retires every parked Work and permanently kills a carved-out question, undisclosed and unpinned
findings.evidence: MEASURED through the real door, every case in its own rolled-back transaction, against a fixture document storing `invoice.total` text `RM 880.00` / cents 88000, `invoice.currency` `MYR`, `invoice.vendor_name` `ACME SDN BHD`, `invoice.invoice_date` `2026-01-02`. The guard behaves EXACTLY as `clara._fact_value_changed` documents itself (normalised cents when both sides carry them, otherwise trimmed text) -- REFUSED `CLR10 value_unchanged`: `RM 880.00 -> 880.00`, `-> 880.0`, `-> RM 880.00`, vendor name to itself, vendor name with surrounding whitespace, `MYR -> MYR`, `2026-01-02 -> 2026-01-02`. ACCEPTED as changes: `RM 880.00 -> 881.00` (the control), `ACME SDN BHD -> Acme Sdn Bhd` (CASE), `MYR -> myr` (CASE), and `2026-01-02 -> 02/01/2026` (the SAME calendar day respelled). Also measured: `present -> empty` is refused by 0217's own pre-existing `value_blank`, not by this guard, and a field with no prior region is always a change (`v_prior_value is not null` gates the guard) -- `invoice.customer_name -> 'NEW BUYER'` ACCEPTED. The asymmetry is inherent and defensible: money has a normalised stored form (cents) and a date does not (`text_content` only, `monetary_cents` null), and case can be a genuine correction. THE POINT IS THE BLAST RADIUS, not the rule: an edit that moves no fact -- a date respelled to the same day, a currency code re-cased -- still advances `facts_version`, retires every Work parked on a question about that document, and makes a #676-carved-out question PERMANENTLY unanswerable (`max(recorded_at)` can never fall back below the question's `created_at`). That is the same consequence the round just spent a commit removing from the identical-value case. Nothing names the limit: 0268's header paragraph says only "a keystroke is not a correction", `packages/db/README.md`'s 0268 section does not mention it, `wave2-lane09-fix.md` §7 lists three other limits and not this one, and `w885.noop.refused` drives only exact-equality cases (the round's own §7 already concedes the text arm is exercised only through a real `invoice.currency` change).
findings.required_fix: State the limit where it will be read -- 0268's header beside the guard, and the report's unverified list: the guard refuses an edit that is equal under `clara._fact_value_changed`, and a cosmetically-equivalent edit that is NOT equal under that rule (case, a date respelled, a currency re-cased) still carries the full retirement and the permanent refusal. Add one cell driving a case-only edit so the behaviour is pinned rather than discovered. Do NOT widen the rule without the owner: case-folding a vendor name would swallow real corrections.

summary: THIRD RECHECK of riders/w2-lane09 at head c5c408455, everything below done rather than read. THE BLOCKER IS CLOSED, and I proved it independently rather than re-running the round's script. In ONE transaction that was then rolled back I rebuilt the exact pre-0268 catalog by re-applying the creating migrations' own statements -- `clara._work_question_record` from 0265, `clara.answer_work_question` from 0200, `clara.revise_document_fact` from 0217 -- and each landed on the literal 0268 pins it (`f4b62dd26d7e0acf`, `15a82c080d102e61`, `b89a01ba9b5f0294`), with no `#885` and no `source_corrected_at` anywhere; I dropped all five routines 0268 creates and deleted its ledger row, then ran 0268 VERBATIM: §0 PRESTATE passed on the first-apply path, and the rest of the file (body + §T tail census) applied, leaving the cohort at 5/5 routines and all three bodies carrying the marker. The rollback control shows all three live bodies unmoved and the ledger row back with checksum `93703b0eaa233e28…`, which equals the file's own sha256 (verified for all four migrations: 0265 `3e35a42c…`, 0266 `ed81bcd8…`, 0267 `5340c2dc…`, 0268 `93703b0e…`, all matching the ledger). THE PIN AUDIT HOLDS, and I exercised every branch the lane database does not exercise today: 0265's redo branch REFUSES CLR10 on today's catalog (as the lane claims, by design) while its first-apply branch PASSES once `_work_question_record` is rewound to 0180's body (sha `cb57a131…`, exactly its pin); 0266's redo branch REFUSES (`does not resolve at its nine-argument signature`); 0267 is bimodal and BOTH branches pass -- the redo branch against today's eleven-argument door, and the first-apply branch after rewinding `list_accounting_work` to 0266's nine-argument door with its posture restored (my first attempt refused, correctly, because the rewind had dropped the ACL -- 0267's prestate checks owner, secdef, config AND acl before the drop, which is stronger than the audit table claims); 0268's three marker-tolerant pins take the marker branch on every redo and their sha branch is the rewind proof above. CATALOG: every door 0265-0268 recuts or creates is owned by `clara_fn_owner` with `search_path=clara, pg_temp` and its ACL unchanged -- `revise_document_fact`/`answer_work_question`/`get_work_question`/`get_work_pending_question` to `clara_authenticated`, `list_accounting_work`/`get_accounting_work_row` to `clara_authenticated` and still SECURITY INVOKER with `plan_cache_mode=force_custom_plan` as 0266 requires, and all five `_`-prefixed helpers ungranted (owner only), including the new `clara._fact_value_changed(jsonb,jsonb)`, which is `language sql immutable`, pure, and correctly NOT security definer since it touches no relation. THE NO-OP REFUSAL, judged as a product change: it is a behaviour change on a human door that the ticket did not ask for, and it is the right one, with two caveats recorded as findings. "Unchanged" is decided on the stored value exactly as `clara._fact_value_changed` documents -- normalised cents when both sides carry them, otherwise trimmed text -- and I drove all fourteen cases the ask names; money respelled three ways, identical text, and surrounding whitespace are refused `CLR10 value_unchanged`, while a CASE change, a currency re-cased and a date respelled to the same calendar day are accepted as changes, `present -> empty` hits 0217's older `value_blank`, and a field with no prior region is always a change. It is NOT an existence oracle: the guard sits at 0268:735, below `clara._human_ctx(role_rank('bookkeeper'))` at :578 and below the `clara.documents` read and `d.firm_id <> c.firm` tenancy check at :604-608, and driven, firm B's bookkeeper gets `CLR11 document_not_found` for an unchanged value, for a changed value, and for a uuid no document has -- three byte-identical refusals. CALLERS: exactly one in the estate. `apps/web/lib/documents/doors.ts` -> `document-revision-dialog.tsx`, which renders the door's message VERBATIM (`setErr(e.message)`) as it does for every other typed refusal on this door, and the db sentence is actionable; no runtime, chat or Work tool calls it (grepped). NO SHIPPED FLOW relied on re-saving the same value: the dialog's only purpose is revision, the e2e walk always changes the value, and the one thing that did rely on it was a test leg (`p646.replay.one_receipt`) which the round converted to a real change. THE TWO ARMS AGREE WITH THE DOORS, measured at the db seam and read at the surface: the carve-out Work answers `work_posted=true` -> `convergeSourceCorrectedPosted` ("use Cancel Work"), `offersRestateFor` false, `restate_accounting_work` refuses `not_restatable status=completed`, `cancel_agent_task` ACCEPTED; the retired Work answers `work_posted=false` -> `convergeSourceCorrected`, `offersRestateFor` false (via `work_status=stopping`), `cancel_agent_task` ACCEPTED -- but `restate_accounting_work` refuses it too, which the round's own table denies (finding L09-RC3-01; the shipped sentence and controls are nevertheless correct, because neither names nor offers a restatement there). GATES, all re-run here: db battery under the exact 54-module gate chain on clara_l09 (work-question-admitted-basis + work-question-reads + work-question + work-list + client-work-pack + work-source-correction-supersede + rig-docs-source-revision + preintegration-gate-chain + web-reads-and-doors + operation-census + rig-isolation) = 187 tests, 186 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, zero `not ok`, and the skip is confirmed rig-isolation T19 (needs CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET); the six touched/affected web unit files = 74/74; the WHOLE apps/web suite = 4776 tests, 4774 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped, exit 0, zero `not ok`; `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm lint` exit 0; `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` exit 1 on exactly one case, the freeze-lint `--retire`-under-CI selftest, with `git diff BASE..HEAD -- scripts/check-frozen-workflows*.mjs` still empty. `git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD unmoved at c5c408455. Nothing above minor remains: two minors (a false door claim in the record, and the undisclosed blast radius of a cosmetically-equivalent edit) and two notes.

ruling_885.delivered: Unchanged from recheck 2 and re-confirmed here at the surface seam. The ruling's non-negotiable half holds for both populations: nobody can answer a question asked against a corrected reading, whether the Work was retired or deliberately carved out, and no arm re-admits, so no pre-correction figure can reach the ledger through this door. What round three adds is that the two arms now tell the person something true and offer only controls the doors accept -- the carve-out arm names Cancel Work and withholds restate on the measured fact `work_posted`, and the retired arm offers no control that would refuse. And a keystroke that changes nothing is no longer a correction at all, so the retirement and the permanent refusal can no longer be triggered by an edit that moves no value under the rule.
ruling_885.replaced_by: 'Re-admitted ON THE CORRECTED FACTS' remains replaced, on every arm, by 'RETIRED, and the person states the instruction again on the corrected document' -- as a fresh admission, since the restatement door refuses a retired Work as well as a posted one. The receipt keeps the two reasons a human is owed (`interpreted_basis`, `basis_predates_correction`). On the carve-out arm nothing is retired; only the answer is refused.
ruling_885.honest_minimum: Yes, and unchanged: re-deriving a basis in SQL is not constructible (`journalBasisSchema` has no back-link from a line to a document field path) and admitting a successor 'in a state that cannot post' is not constructible either (`clara.open_work_question` raises CLR13 `task_not_running` on a queued task, 0184). No frozen body was touched; the freeze-lint chain is green.
ruling_885.remainder: Unchanged from recheck 2, and the lane's contract for it is still adequate. (1) RE-ADMISSION ON THE CORRECTED FACTS, contracted for the wave-4 chatTurn_v22 / claraWork_v6 cut: WHO (the Work runtime), WHAT (per retired Work, enqueue a re-read with the same client, purpose and source_refs, initiated by the correcting actor), FROM WHAT (the live clara.document_regions of the newest done extraction, never the retired basis), THROUGH WHICH DOOR (clara.admit_journal_work then clara.open_work_question naming BOTH figures, nothing posting until answered), and the link it claims (the cancellation's op key, which is why superseded_by is left NULL). (2) 'Needs-you shows the replacement' is not deliverable before (1). (3) A first-class retirement reason instead of a derived op key (L09-SPEC-07), owed to #840's feed. (4) Correcting a posted result (#676), parked by docs/PRD.md. Nothing in this recheck's findings belongs to the remainder: both minors are a record correction and a disclosure, and neither blocks the merge.
